M Faruque, Deputy Attorney-General, with Mohammad Mushfiqur Rahman Khan, Asstt. Attorney-General and MA Rouf, Asstt. Attorney-General — For the Petitioner.

Muzibur Rahman, Advocate — For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Middle East Garments ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque J : This Rule was issued at the instance of the respondent petitioner calling upon the opposite party Middle East Garments to show cause as to why judgment and order dt. 30-5-96 passed by the Addl. Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong in Criminal. Appeal No. 215 of 1995 setting aside orders dated 13-6-95 and 9-9-95 passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong in Misc. Case No. 321 of 1995 should not be set aside. 

 4. It appears from the impugned judgment that the learned Addl. Session Judge held that admittedly appellant opposite party has got a licence from the licensing authority for using the building as Workshop of the Garment Factory Magistrate was bound to issue a notice and simultaneously take possession of the building and articles stored therein, that complaint must be made by the Director of fire service, petition of complaint dated 7-6-95 before the chief Metropolitan Magistrate upon which Misc. Case No. 321 of 1995 was initiated was not a proper complaint under section 15A of the said ordinance, Magistrate had no authority to delegate his power to take possession of the Factory and the articles stored in the Factory to the officer in charge, Panchlaish PS and the Magistrate also committed illegality by not giving any copy of the complaint with the notice and not fixing any time to show cause by the opposite party and thereby violated the provisions of sub section (2) of the said section 15A of the said Ordinance. Court below further ever ruled the objection regarding filing of the appeal before the Sessions Judge instead of the Distt. Judge on the ground that the same person was holding both the offices. 

 5. It appears from sub-section (2) of section 42 of the said Ordinance that Director may, subject to the prior approval of the Government, delegate any of his powers,duties and functions under this Ordinance to any officer or officers subordinate to him. In exercise of that power by Notification dated 23rd July 1971, Director with the approval of the Government delegated certain powers to his subordinates including the Ware Houses Inspectors who have been authorised to institute and conduct court cases against the defaulters for penal action under section 15A, 23-33, 35, and 36. In view of such delegation learned Additional Sessions Judge was not justified in holding that the petition of complaint before the Magistrate was not proper complaint under section 15A of the said Ordinance. 

 8. Now coming to the crux of the question as to maintainability of the appeal, on going through the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 15A we do not find mention of the word ''order" therein. On the other hand we find mention of the word ''Order" in sub-section (3) thereof. Sub section (4) of said section provides that an appeal shall lie with the District Judge from "an order of such Magistrate" if presented within 30 days from the dated of the order. There is nothing before us to show when the opposite party applied for the certified copy of the impugned orders and when the same was obtained. In calculating 30 days from the date of order time spent for obtaining the certified copy for preferring the appeal would be excluded from the time of making the order by the Magistrate and presentation of the Memo of appeal. In the absence of anything to show to that effect it is difficult for us to hold that the appeal preferred by the opposite party was not within time. But as noticed above we find that an appeal lies only against in "order" made by the Magistrate on consideration of the cause shown after taking evidence. In the instant case admittedly on 13-6-95 notice was directed to be issued on the opposite party and OC Panchlaish PS was directed to take possession of the articles with the building and then on 9-9-95 Mr AR Chakma Metropolitan Magistrate, attached to WASA Chittagong was directed to remain present at the time of taking delivery of possession as prayed for by the OC. Though in common parlance such directions are termed as orders of the Magistrate it is to be seen whether in the absence of the word "Order" in sub section (2) of section 15A the same can be treated as "order" contemplated under sub-section (4) of the said section. Though the opposite party had shown cause against the notice issued by the Magistrate partly denying the allegations and partly admitting the same evidence was not taken by the Magistrate in support of the respective case of the parties. As the Magistrate did not make any "order" on consideration of the cause shown and any evidence, forfeiting all or any of the articles and relinquishing the possession of the building or releasing the articles not forfeited, no question of preferring an appeal by the opposite party under sub-section (4) or section 15A could arise. In that view of the matter we find merit in the contention raised by the learned Deputy Attorney-General as to the maintainability of the appeal and no merit in the submission of the learned Advocate for the opposite party in this respect. On consideration of the entire matter we are of the view that an appeal lies under sub-section (4) of section 15A only when a reasoned order under sub section (3) is made by the Magistrate after taking over possession of the building along with the articles stored therein under sub-section (2) of the said section and showing of cause by the opposite party on receipt of the notice and taking of evidence forfeiting all or any of the articles seized and not against any direction under sub-section (2) of the said section even if such direction for issuance of notice or taking over possession of any building with the articles lying therein under that sub-section could be termed as an "Order" as the same is not reasoned one on consideration of evidence but casual one made ex parte. So we hold that the appeal before the learned Sessions Judge was not maintainable against the direction issuing notice on 13-6-95 and further direction made on 9-9-95 asking a Magistrate to remain present at the time of taking over possession by the OC. 

 9. In view of our above finding we need not enter into the merit of the case decided by the learned Additional Sessions Judge though we are of the view that he ought not to have decided the same without any evidence prejudicing the parties before the Magistrate. Those findings of the Additional Sessions Judge regarding the merit of the case will not be binding on the Magistrate in deciding the case under sub-section (3) of the section 15A after taking evidence. But before doing so possession of the building with the articles lying therein must be taken over.
